name: @w6w-apps/wrike
description: Manage Wrike tasks, folders/projects, comments, contacts and timelogs.

w6w.longDescription:
Wrike is a work-management platform organized around a folder tree: spaces contain projects and folders, which contain tasks, which carry comments, timelogs and attachments. This app covers that core surface end to end — creating, searching, updating and deleting tasks and folders/projects, reading and posting comments, reading and updating contacts (Wrike's term for users and groups), and recording or editing timelogs — plus read access to attachment metadata and download links.

Wrike's API v4 is unusual among REST APIs: every mutating request (POST/PUT) passes its whole payload as query-string parameters, not a JSON body, with arrays and objects JSON-encoded inline inside the query value. Every action in this app builds requests that way, matching Wrike's own OpenAPI definitions rather than the more common JSON-body convention. Wrike also serves customer data from one of three fixed regional hosts (US, EU, US2); the Connection records which one, and every action reads it from there rather than guessing.

Health checks track credential liveness via Wrike's lightweight, scope-free /version endpoint and the connected account's own suspension flag. Wrike publishes no machine-readable status feed and no rate-limit headroom, and both are declared as such rather than guessed at.
